subject: Storage for paperwork and equipment
hook: Behind a tidy home office wall: drilled shelf rows and planned cable routes.
ig:
Behind a tidy home office wall: drilled shelf rows and planned cable routes.

A home office storage wall looks simple when the doors are shut. The work is in what you cannot see. How we work:

- Panels cut to fit your room on our sliding table panel saw.
- Shelf-pin rows drilled on the multi-spindle boring machine, so shelves can move as your files and books change.
- Cable routes planned at the design stage, with grommets where the printer, router and chargers will sit.
- Units assembled and checked in our Hanley workshop. Not flat-pack.
- Fitted by our own team, cables fed through before the doors go on.

The cable planning is the bit people forget. Leave it to fitting day and you end up drilling holes in a finished cupboard.

If a better workspace is on your list for 2027, DM us OFFICE and we will send over the details.
fb:
A tidy home office is mostly about the bits you never see.

In our Hanley workshop, a storage wall starts with panels cut to your room, shelf-pin rows drilled so the shelves can move as your needs change, and holes for cable grommets planned exactly where the printer and router will go. Then it is assembled, checked and fitted by our own team.

Getting the cables right at the design stage is what stops the trailing-wire look.
